topics.title: Comprehension, Essay Writing, Sound System, Grammar, and Translation

subtopics.content: Reading comprehension, essay/letter writing, Efik phonetics/phonology, word structures, grammatical categories, translation
subtopics.objective: Answer comprehension passage questions[cite: 240]; write 300-word narrative, descriptive, argumentative, expository, debate, or letter essays in standard orthography[cite: 241, 242]; identify Efik vowels, consonants, environments of occurrence, loanword adaptation, tone, and intonation[cite: 242]; analyze word roots, affixes, reduplication, word classes, grammatical categories (tense, negation), phrases, and sentence structures[cite: 242]; translate expressions accurately[cite: 241].

sections.sectionTitle: Section B: Literature (Mbuk Ye Uto Efik)

topics.title: Literary Principles, Prescribed Oral and Written Literature (Prose, Poetry, Drama)

subtopics.content: Basic literary devices, prescribed Efik oral folktales/poetry/traditional drama, prescribed written Efik novels, selected poems, and plays
subtopics.objective: Apply literary appreciation principles[cite: 241]; evaluate prescribed oral literature texts (*Inyan Abasi Ndem*, *Mutanda Oyom Namondo*, *Nkpon Udan*)[cite: 247, 249]; critique prescribed written prose texts (*Edikot Ñwed Mbuk 6*, *Obufa Edikot Ñwed 6*)[cite: 247, 249]; analyze designated Efik poem selections (*Ufok-Uto Iko Efik*, *Ñkpasip Ñkpo Kiet*)[cite: 247, 249]; analyze set written plays (*Sidibe*, *Iduo Owo*, *Ansa Udo Enañ*)[cite: 245, 247, 249].

sections.sectionTitle: Section C: Culture (Edu Uwem Ye Mme Nka Ke Efik)

subtopics.content: Occupations, child upbringing, traditional foods/cooking, libation, family setup, worship (Abasi, Ndem), proverbs, kingship (Ubọn), secret societies
subtopics.objective: Examine traditional occupations (fishing, farming, crafts), child discipline, local food preparation (fufu, ekpañ ñkukwo), and libation practices[cite: 243]; analyze family structures (Ubon/Ekpuk), religious worship systems (Abasi, Ndem, Ibok), Efik proverbs (Nke), Kingship institution (Ubọn), and traditional secret societies[cite: 244].
